Fourteen comments

Viva la Altan

here’s my first submission in ABC, hope I haven’t totally botched it. Coming soon, the Glory Reel.

↳ Posted by emily_bmore on December 29th, 2002.

James Kelly does a really lovely setting of this one on his perhaps less than creatively named “Traditional Irish Music” -- it’s on the first track along with a Gan Ainm and Lads of Laois and has been on my list of tunes to learn for quite some time. At some point, I’ll try and transcribe the Kelly setting and post it here.

Zina

↳ Posted by Zina Lee on January 1st, 2003.

Well, here it is, such as it is -- I’m still not real great at the whole ABC thing. Plus, of course, trying to transcribe James Kelly’s settings is trying to hit a moving target -- possible, but there’s always something else he’s doing that you just can’t quite catch…

↳ Posted by Taranis on January 28th, 2014.

The Heathery Cruach, X:4

This is a version based on Cathal Hayden’s playing that I got from fiddler Ross Couper. In the video above Cathal sometimes plays a D triplet instead of DA,D in the first bar. Whistle/pipes/flute can play the triplet or just the A, up an octave.

Absolutely love John Doherty’s version of this on “Bundle and Go”.. It’s slightly different though. A lot of the A’s are G’s in his version which lends it a different feel.

Re: The Heathery Cruach

According to P.W.Joyce, 1887,
a cruach is a rick or piled- up hill.

(Perhaps the type of hill which is heart-breaking to ascend because there is always another horizon after the one you’ve just reached?)
